gold.question: Regarding PV-2-1 on the P&ID: The valve leaks through when shut. Is it the seat ring or the plug seal, and how do I check?

candidate: Not in the documents. PV-2-1 is a globe-style control valve (Fisher ET/EAT type per its datasheet). In this design the shutoff when closed is made at the seat: for metal-seat construction the plug closes against the seat ring, and for the standard PTFE (soft) seat construction the seal is a PTFE disk/disk-seat assembly at the seat; the valve plug seal is a separate seal that bears against the cage (balancing the plug) and is not the primary shutoff element — except on TSO (tight shutoff) trim, where the protected soft seat plus plug seal provide Class V shutoff. So a leak-through when shut is most likely at the seat ring/soft seat (e.g., worn PTFE disk, damaged seat surface, or insufficient seat load), not the plug seal. The datasheet does not contain a field inspection/leak-check procedure — the only leakage check mentioned is the factory test (TSO trim: no leakage at shipment, water as test medium; shutoff classes per ANSI/FCI 70-2 / IEC 60534-4, Class IV standard for metal seat, Class V/VI optional). To check, you would isolate the valve, pressurize upstream, and observe downstream leakage, then inspect the seat ring/PTFE disk and plug seal ring at overhaul — but the specific step-by-step procedure is not in the documents.

Levels: default high >= 21.75 mA (>= 22.5 mA with M6, DA1, T9, RK), low <= 3.75 mA; NAMUR >= 22.5 / <= 3.6 mA; custom 20.2-23.0 / 3.6-3.8 mA.
